messages.subject: apparent Date bug in plyr 0.1.9
parts:
Hi Hadley et al.,

> dd <- data.frame(x=c('a','a'), y=as.Date(c('2010-01-01', '2010-02-02')), z=c(1,2))
> ddply(dd, .(x), function(q) {q})
Error in NextMethod(.Generic) : no method to invoke

Enter a frame number, or 0 to exit

1: ddply(dd, .(x), function(q) {
2: ldply(.data = pieces, .fun = .fun, ..., .progress = .progress)
3: list_to_dataframe(res, attr(.data, "split_labels"))
4: rbind.fill(res)
5: `[<-`(`*tmp*`, , value = NA)
6: .Primitive("[<-")(x, ..., value = value)
7: `[<-.Date`(x, ..., value = value)
8: NextMethod(.Generic)

Selection: 0
> dd <- data.frame(x=c('a','a'), y=c('2010-01-01', '2010-02-02'), z=c(1,2))
> ddply(dd, .(x), function(q) {q})
x y z
1 a 2010-01-01 1
2 a 2010-02-02 2

I can work around this, if necessary, but would obviously prefer not
to...

Thanks!

-Harlan

messages.subject: Re: apparent Date bug in plyr 0.1.9
parts: This is weird. I've identified it as a problem with the "rv" package:

> ddply(dd, .(x), function(q) {q})
  x          y z
1 a 2010-01-01 1
2 a 2010-02-02 2

> library(rv)
Package rv loaded.

Attaching package: 'rv'


    The following object(s) are masked from package:stats :

     cor,
     cov,
     sd,
     var


    The following object(s) are masked from package:graphics :

     abline,
     plot

> ddply(dd, .(x), function(q) {q})
Error in NextMethod(.Generic) : no method to invoke

How could rv break plyr if it's not masking any of plyr's objects?

 -Harlan

messages.author: 9e1d805a26f6d719
messages.subject: Re: apparent Date bug in plyr 0.1.9
parts:
FYI, yes, it was rv that was doing weird things with generics so that 1 + rvobject and c(1, rvobject) will work. I've given up on the rv package and rewrote (some of) it using proto objects. I lose all of the nice operator overloading, so I have to write rvobj1$plus(rvobj2) or rvobject$c(1), but at least it doesn't break anything!

I'm likely to rewrite rv in Scala too. Looking forward to implicit conversions to solve this problem!

 -Harlan
